chunks: 3046 - The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله offered two rams as sacrifice. He slaughtered one with his own hand and said: “O Allah, this is on behalf of me and on behalf of those of my Ahl al-Bayt who did not offer a sacrifice.” Then he slaughtered the other and said: “O Allah, this is on behalf of me and on behalf of those of my Ummah who did not offer a sacrifice.”
And Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام would offer a sacrifice on behalf of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله every year with a ram; he would slaughter it and say:

“In the Name of Allah: ‘I have turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, inclining upright,’ submitting, ‘and I am not among the polytheists.’ ‘Indeed, my salat (prayer), my sacrifice, my living, and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.’ O Allah, from You and for You.”
Then he would say: “O Allah, this is on behalf of Your Prophet.” Then he would slaughter it, and he would slaughter another ram on behalf of himself.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِي: my household, referring to the Prophet’s family
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: those who associate partners with Allah
key_terms.كَبْشَيْنِ: two rams used for the sacrifice
key_terms.مِنْكَ وَلَكَ: from You and for You, expressing that the offering is by Allah’s provision and for His sake
key_terms.نُسُكِي: my sacrificial rite or act of worship

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام perform the Eid sacrifice and what did they recite?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the sacrificial practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, who offered on behalf of himself, his Ahl al-Bayt, and members of his Ummah who had not offered a sacrifice. It also records that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام continued to sacrifice annually on behalf of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, reciting Quranic words of tawhid, sincerity, and devotion to Allah.
